    Rule-Strategy Catalog — Configuration and Structural Levels

    • Date: 2026-07-11
    • Traded market: BTCUSDT 5m base timeframe (three cross-asset strategies trade ETHUSDT with BTCUSDT as context; several strategies read higher-timeframe 4h/1d context).
    • Purpose: the definitive catalog of the 51 rule-based strategies — for each one, how it is implemented in Layer-1 (entry rules) and Layer-2 (management profile), and the stop/target level it uses, grounded in the strategy's canonical source (book / paper / authoritative reference).

    1. How a strategy is built

    Every strategy is a RuleStrategySpec = Layer-1 entry rules + a Layer-2 management profile + parameters (scripts/experiments/generate/rule_strategies/).

    • Layer-1 (entry rules). An ordered list of {expression, signal} rules over the strategy's raw features. The first rule whose DSL expression is true emits its market-view signal (LONG / SHORT); when none match, the default signal (NONE) holds. Newest closed bar is offset {-1}; window functions read a range {-A:-B} (highest, lowest, avg, std, percentile, slope, count, any, cross_up, cross_down, max, min, abs).
    • Layer-2 (management profile). One of eight profiles emits the post-open action_rules — the stop, target, partials, pyramiding, trailing and time-stops.

    1.1 The eight bot profiles and the management each emits

    Code Profile Management
    BO breakout structural stop inside the broken range (when supplied); no-follow-through time-stop (6 bars / +0.1R); partial 50% at +1.5R; optional wide ATR trail
    TR trend_rider break-even move at +1R; pyramid at +2R (≤ 2 legs); optional wide ATR trail; stop/target from the tuned config
    PB pullback structural stop beyond the pullback swing (when supplied); partial 50% at +2R; optional wide ATR trail
    MR mean_reversion structural target at the reversion mean + structural stop beyond the extreme (when supplied); stalled-trade time-stop (24 bars)
    IN intraday structural stop at the intraday reference (when supplied); partial 50% at +1R; force-flat at 20:00 UTC session close
    FR failure_reversal structural stop beyond the failure extreme (when supplied); first target 50% at +1R; runner extended to +2R; time-stop (8 bars)
    HY regime_hybrid trend-style management (break-even at +1R, pyramiding, optional trail); the regime routing lives in Layer-1
    SP spread_pairs deferred — needs coordinated two-leg execution

    1.2 Level ownership (structural vs tuned default)

    The tuned stop-loss, take-profit and trailing stop live as plain numbers in bot_config.strategy_config. A profile places a structural level only when the strategy's own logic defines one (the broken range low, the reversion mean, the indicator line): it passes a DSL expression to SET_ENTRY_LEVELS, which decorates the model-driven open. When a level is omitted, the engine falls back to the tuned config. entry below denotes position_entry_price{-1}; atr denotes market_atr{-1}.

    1.3 The level each strategy uses, by canonical group

    Grounded in each strategy's source, the level falls into four groups:

    1. Breakout / channel → structural stop inside the broken range (or the Turtle 2N ATR stop).
    2. Mean-reversion → structural target at the mean (band middle, moving average, z-score→0).
    3. Stop-and-reverse indicators (Supertrend, Parabolic SAR) → the indicator line is the stop, trailing every bar.
    4. Pure oscillator recross / signal crossover / momentum-sign / cross-asset rotation → no intrinsic price level; the canonical exit is the opposite signal (already in Layer-1), so the tuned config stop/target governs the trade.

    1.4 Why these 51 strategies were chosen

    The catalog is not arbitrary. It is the implementable set of the strategy-first research catalog docs/_researchs/_RULE_BASED/20260621_02_Fifty Rule-Defined Trading Strategies for Rainbow Trader.md (companion audit 20260621_01), chosen against three criteria:

    1. Span the canonical families of classical systematic trading. The catalog deliberately covers the whole spectrum — trend/breakout (the most evidence-backed family: time-series momentum and Donchian/ Turtle channel breakouts have the deepest academic and practitioner record), momentum and relative-strength, mean-reversion (oscillator and band reversion), volatility/structure (squeezes, bar patterns, failed breakouts), regime-gated trend, session/VWAP, and cross-asset. The point is coverage: learn which kind of strategy fits which market regime, not to bet on one system.
    2. Be expressible on the shipped engine. Each strategy maps onto the two-layer rule engine (Layer-1 entry rules + Layer-2 profile) using the shipped DSL primitives and the 34 indicators. The research catalog wrote every rule in pseudocode precisely so it could be mapped onto real feature names; the few entries that need engine capabilities that do not exist yet are called out in §11.
    3. Stress the rule primitives. The mix was picked to exercise every primitive that matters — windows, crosses, slopes, percentiles, higher-timeframe and context-symbol features, regime gating — so the engine and DSL get validated across the full surface, not just one happy path.

    The research catalog defines ~50 strategies and grades each by evidence strength; 51 experiments were implemented (the directly-expressible set, including a few close variants). One catalog entry — the spread/pairs z-score reversion — was deliberately not implemented: it needs coordinated two-leg execution the single-instrument engine does not support, so it is not among the 51 (its profile exists only as a stub that raises NotImplementedError).

    2. Trend / breakout family

    2.1 donchian_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > highest(high{-20:-2}); SHORT close{-1} < lowest(low{-20:-2}). The 20-bar channel break is the entry.
    • L2: breakout() — no-follow time-stop, 50% partial at +1.5R.
    • Level (source: Curtis Faith, Way of the Turtle, Turtle System 1; tradingblox.com): stop at 2N, i.e. 2× the channel ATR from entry → entry − 2·atr (long) / entry + 2·atr (short). No fixed target; the canonical System-1 exit is the opposite 10-bar channel, a trailing/reversal mechanic.

    2.2 turtle_breakout — profile TR

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > highest(high{-55:-2}); SHORT close{-1} < lowest(low{-55:-2}). The 55-bar System-2 channel break.
    • L2: trend_rider() — break-even at +1R, pyramiding ≤ 2 legs.
    • Level (source: Faith, Way of the Turtle, System 2; litefinance.org): stop at 2N → entry − 2·atr / entry + 2·atr (identical to System 1). No fixed target (opposite 20-bar channel exit).

    2.3 adx_di_surge — profile TR

    • L1: LONG +DI{-1} > −DI{-1} and ADX{-1} > 25 and ADX{-1} > ADX{-5}; SHORT mirrored on −DI.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, Directional Movement / Extreme Point Rule): stop at the signal bar's extreme → low{-1} (long) / high{-1} (short). No fixed target; exit on the opposite DI crossover.

    2.4 ema_crossover — profile TR

    • L1: LONG cross_up(ema20, ema50) and ADX{-1} > 20; SHORT cross_down(ema20, ema50) and ADX{-1} > 20.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Kaufman, Trading Systems and Methods): no intrinsic price level — a moving-average cross is a direction filter whose canonical exit is the opposite cross. Uses the tuned config stop/target.

    2.5 sma_regime_cross — profile TR

    • L1: LONG cross_up(sma50, sma200); SHORT cross_down(sma50, sma200) — the golden / death cross.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: standard 50/200 convention): no intrinsic level; opposite-cross exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    2.6 triple_ema_alignment — profile TR

    • L1: LONG ema10 > ema20 > ema50 and slope(ema50{-10:-1}) > 0 and close > ema10; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: GMMA / Guppy is a different 12-EMA structure; no canonical stop for this 10/20/50 construction): no intrinsic level; loss of alignment is the exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    2.7 aroon_trend_emergence — profile TR

    • L1: LONG aroon_up{-1} > 70 and aroon_down{-1} < 30 and aroon_up{-1} > aroon_up{-5}; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Tushar Chande, original Aroon, 1995; StockCharts): no intrinsic level — Aroon is a trend-emergence filter, not a full system. Tuned config stop/target.

    2.8 linreg_slope_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG slope(linreg{-10:-1}) > 0 and close{-1} > linreg{-1}; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: eSignal linear-regression-channel doc): no intrinsic level — the channel stop/target convention is for reversion trades inside std-dev bands, which this no-band trend break does not compute. Tuned config stop/target.

    2.9 ema200_pullback_continuation — profile PB

    • L1: LONG htf_close{-1} > htf_ema200{-1} and low{-1} <= ema20{-1} and close{-1} > ema20{-1} and rsi{-1} > 50; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: pullback() — 50% partial at +2R.
    • Level (source: Alexander Elder, Triple Screen, Trading for a Living): stop below the recent pullback swing → lowest(low{-3:-1}) (long) / highest(high{-3:-1}) (short). No fixed target (trailed out).

    2.10 supertrend_flip — profile TR

    • L1: LONG cross_up(close, supertrend.line) and supertrend.direction{-1} == 1; SHORT mirrored on direction 0.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Olivier Seban, SuperTrend, 2009; luxalgo.com, trendspider.com): the Supertrend line IS the stop, trailing every bar → initial stop supertrend.line{-1}, re-trailed to it each bar. No separate target; the position flips on the opposite cross.

    2.11 ichimoku_cloud_breakout — profile TR

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > max(senkou_a, senkou_b) and tenkan{-1} > kijun{-1} and close{-1} > close{-27}; SHORT mirrored with min(...).
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Goichi Hosoda Ichimoku Kinko Hyo; xs.com): stop at the near cloud edge → min(senkou_a, senkou_b){-1} (long) / max(senkou_a, senkou_b){-1} (short). No fixed target (trend reversal exit).

    3. Momentum family

    3.1 time_series_momentum — profile TR

    • L1: LONG roc63{-1} > 0 and roc21{-1} > 0; SHORT both < 0.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, Time Series Momentum, SSRN): no intrinsic level — risk is ex-ante volatility sizing and the sign flip at rebalance. Tuned config stop/target.

    3.2 multi_horizon_momentum — profile TR

    • L1: LONG roc21 > 0 and roc63 > 0 and roc126 > 0; SHORT all < 0.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Moskowitz et al.; Clenow, Following the Trend): no intrinsic level; vol-scaled sizing, horizon-sign exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    3.3 roc_acceleration_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG roc{-1} > roc{-5} and roc{-1} > 0 and close{-1} > highest(high{-10:-2}); SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Turtle Donchian / Darvas box, thepatternsite.com): stop inside the broken 10-bar range → lowest(low{-10:-2}) (long) / highest(high{-10:-2}) (short). No fixed target.

    3.4 ppo_zero_line — profile TR

    • L1: LONG cross_up(ppo.line, 0) and ppo.line{-1} > ppo.signal{-1}; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Gerald Appel PPO; StockCharts): no intrinsic level; opposite-crossover exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    3.5 trix_trend — profile TR

    • L1: LONG cross_up(trix.value, trix.signal) and trix.value{-1} > 0; SHORT mirrored below 0.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Jack Hutson TRIX; StockCharts): no intrinsic level; opposite signal-line cross exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    3.6 mfi_momentum_continuation — profile PB

    • L1: LONG mfi{-1} > 60 and mfi{-1} > mfi{-5} and close{-1} > ema20{-1}; SHORT mirrored (< 40).
    • L2: pullback().
    • Level (source: Quong & Soudack MFI; StockCharts): no intrinsic level — the 60/40 continuation gate is a house construction; MFI defines no stop, and no swing point is referenced. Tuned config stop/target.

    3.7 volume_impulse_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > highest(high{-15:-2}) and volume{-1} > 1.8·avg(volume{-20:-2}); SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Darvas box / volume-breakout convention): stop inside the broken 15-bar range → lowest(low{-15:-2}) / highest(high{-15:-2}). No fixed target.

    3.8 obv_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > highest(high{-20:-2}) and obv{-1} > highest(obv{-20:-2}); SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Joseph Granville OBV; Turtle channel convention): stop inside the broken 20-bar range → lowest(low{-20:-2}) / highest(high{-20:-2}). No fixed target.

    3.9 mtf_momentum_stack — profile TR

    • L1: LONG htf_roc63 > 0 and mtf_roc21 > 0 and ltf_roc5 > 0; SHORT all < 0 (daily / 4h / 5m).
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Clenow; Moskowitz et al.): no intrinsic level; vol-scaled sizing, cross-timeframe sign exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    4. Mean-reversion family

    4.1 rsi2_dip_buy — profile MR

    • L1: LONG htf_close > htf_ema200 and rsi2{-1} < 10 and close > ema50; SHORT mirrored (rsi2 > 90).
    • L2: mean_reversion() — 24-bar time-stop.
    • Level (source: Connors & Alvarez, Short-Term Trading Strategies That Work): target = the 5-period average → avg(close{-5:-1}). Connors tested fixed stops and found they degrade the system, so no structural stop (config default governs).

    4.2 rsi_range_reversal — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and rsi{-2} < 30 and rsi{-1} > 30; SHORT mirrored (70).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Wilder, New Concepts, RSI): no intrinsic price level — the exit is the opposite RSI extreme recross, an oscillator condition, not a price. Tuned config stop/target.

    4.3 stochastic_reversal — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and %K{-2} < 20 and cross_up(%K, %D); SHORT mirrored (80).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: George Lane's Stochastic; TrendSpider): no intrinsic price level; opposite %K/%D crossover exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    4.4 williams_reversal — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and %R{-2} < −90 and %R{-1} > −80; SHORT mirrored (−10 / −20).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Larry Williams %R; Fidelity): no intrinsic price level; opposite-extreme recross exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    4.5 bollinger_touch_reentry — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and close{-2} < bb.lower{-2} and close{-1} > bb.lower{-1}; SHORT mirrored on bb.upper.
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: John Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands): target = the middle band → bb.middle{-1}. No structural stop in Bollinger's own definition (config default).

    4.6 bollinger_percent_b_snapback — profile MR

    • L1: LONG %b{-2} < 0 and %b{-1} > 0 and zscore(close,20) < −1.5; SHORT mirrored (> 1, > 1.5).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Bollinger %B, StockCharts): target = the middle band → bb.middle{-1} (same reversion premise). Config-default stop.

    4.7 zscore_reversion_to_mean — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and zscore(close,50){-1} < −2 and z rising; SHORT mirrored (> 2, falling).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Ernest Chan, Quantitative Trading; QuantInsti): target = the rolling mean → avg(close{-50:-1}) (z→0); stop at the ~3σ extension → avg(close{-50:-1}) − 3·std(close{-50:-1}) (a widely-cited convention for the family).

    4.8 keltner_channel_fade — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and close{-2} < kc.lower{-2} and close{-1} > kc.lower{-1}; SHORT mirrored on kc.upper.
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Chester Keltner / Linda Raschke; StockCharts): target = the channel middle line → kc.middle{-1}. Config-default stop.

    4.9 cci_extreme_reversal — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and cci{-2} < −100 and cci{-1} > −100; SHORT mirrored (+100).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Donald Lambert CCI; StockCharts): no intrinsic price level — Lambert's system exits on the ±100 recross; the CCI cannot be inverted to a price from the exposed features. Tuned config stop/target.

    4.10 mfi_exhaustion_reversal — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and mfi{-2} < 20 and mfi{-1} > 20; SHORT mirrored (80).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: Quong & Soudack MFI; StockCharts): no intrinsic price level; opposite-threshold recross exit. Tuned config stop/target.

    4.11 consecutive_bar_exhaustion — profile FR

    • L1: LONG count(close{-5:-1} < open{-5:-1}) >= 4 and close{-1} < kc.lower{-1} and close{-1} > open{-1}; SHORT mirrored on kc.upper.
    • L2: failure_reversal() — first partial at +1R, runner to +2R, 8-bar time-stop.
    • Level (source: Connors, High Probability ETF Trading, Multiple-Days-Down/Up): target = the 5-period average → avg(close{-5:-1}). Connors runs the family with no stop (config default).

    4.12 distance_from_ema_reversion — profile MR

    • L1: LONG ranging_gate and pct_distance(close, ema20){-1} < −0.01 and distance contracting; SHORT mirrored (> 0.01).
    • L2: mean_reversion().
    • Level (source: moving-average-envelope reversion convention): target = the reference EMA → ema{-1}. No single canonical stop for this generic family (config default).

    5. Volatility / structure family

    5.1 failed_breakout_reversal — profile FR

    • L1: LONG close{-2} < lowest(low{-20:-3}) and close{-1} > lowest(low{-20:-3}) and close{-1} > open{-1}; SHORT mirrored on the highs.
    • L2: failure_reversal().
    • Level (source: swing-failure / failed-breakout pattern convention): stop beyond the failure wick → lowest(low{-2:-1}) (long) / highest(high{-2:-1}) (short). Target is the generic FR R-multiple.

    5.2 inside_bar_expansion — profile BO

    • L1: inside bar at −2 (high{-2} < high{-3} and low{-2} > low{-3}); LONG close{-1} > high{-2}; SHORT close{-1} < low{-2}.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Toby Crabel; FTMO inside-bar rule): stop beyond the mother bar → low{-3} (long) / high{-3} (short). No fixed target.

    5.3 atr_expansion_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG atr{-1} > 1.3·avg(atr{-20:-2}) and close{-1} > highest(high{-10:-2}); SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Wilder Volatility System + Donchian channel convention): stop at the opposite side of the broken 10-bar channel → lowest(low{-10:-2}) / highest(high{-10:-2}). No fixed target.

    5.4 volatility_contraction_expansion — profile BO

    • L1: LONG volatility{-1} < percentile(volatility{-252:-2},15) and vol rising and close{-1} > highest(high{-10:-2}); SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Mark Minervini VCP; traderlion.com): tight stop below the last contraction, taken as the range-window low → lowest(low{-10:-2}) / highest(high{-10:-2}). No fixed target (trailed).

    5.5 parabolic_sar_reversal — profile TR

    • L1: LONG cross_up(close, sar) and ADX{-1} > 20; SHORT cross_down(close, sar) and ADX{-1} > 20.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Wilder, New Concepts, Parabolic Time/Price): the SAR value IS the stop, trailing every bar → initial stop sar{-1}, re-trailed to it each bar. No separate target (stop-and-reverse).

    5.6 choppiness_release — profile BO

    • L1: LONG chop{-2} > 61.8 and chop{-1} < 50 and close{-1} > highest(high{-10:-2}); SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Bill Dreiss Choppiness Index): no intrinsic level — a pure regime filter, paired with a channel break. Tuned config stop/target.

    5.7 dmi_pullback_continuation — profile PB

    • L1: LONG +DI > −DI and ADX{-1} > 25 and low{-1} <= ema20{-1} and close{-1} > ema20{-1} and close{-1} > open{-1}; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: pullback().
    • Level (source: Wilder, New Concepts, DMI / Extreme Point Rule): stop at the pullback bar's extreme → low{-1} (long) / high{-1} (short). No fixed target (opposite DI cross exit).

    5.8 regime_switch_hybrid — profile HY

    • L1 (first-match): trend leg trending == 1 and confirmed and ema20 > ema50 and close > ema50; range leg ranging == 1 and confirmed and rsi{-2} < 30 and rsi{-1} > 30; mirrored SHORT legs.
    • L2: regime_hybrid().
    • Level (source: composite of MA-trend + Wilder RSI): no intrinsic level for the composite or its building blocks. Tuned config stop/target.

    5.9 bollinger_squeeze_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: LONG bb.bandwidth{-1} < percentile(bb.bandwidth{-252:-2},10) and close{-1} > bb.upper{-1}; SHORT mirrored on bb.lower.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands, Squeeze): stop = the middle band → bb.middle{-1} (a close back through the basis gives back the edge). No fixed target in the primary text.

    5.10 bollinger_keltner_squeeze — profile BO

    • L1: LONG bb inside kc at −2 and released at −1 and roc{-1} > 0; SHORT ... and roc{-1} < 0.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: John Carter, Mastering the Trade, TTM Squeeze): staged ATR targets → first target entry + 2·atr (a second stage at +3 ATR is a second rule). Discretionary stop → config default.

    5.11 nr7_breakout — profile BO

    • L1: nr7 = hl_pct{-1} <= lowest(hl_pct{-7:-1}); LONG nr7 and close{-1} > high{-2}; SHORT nr7 and close{-1} < low{-2}.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: Toby Crabel; StockCharts NR7): stop at the NR7 bar's extreme → low{-1} (long) / high{-1} (short) — a move back through it invalidates the break. No fixed target (fast time exit).

    5.12 pivot_breakout_continuation — profile BO

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > pivots.r1{-1} and vol_surge and daily_close > daily_ema200; SHORT mirrored on pivots.s1.
    • L2: breakout().
    • Level (source: floor-trader pivots; babypips.com): stop just inside the broken level → pivots.r1{-1} / pivots.s1{-1}; target the next pivot out → pivots.r2{-1} / pivots.s2{-1}.

    5.13 fractal_breakout_retest — profile PB

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > fractals.high_level{-1} and any(low{-3:-1} <= fractals.high_level{-1}) and close{-1} > open{-1}; SHORT mirrored on fractals.low_level.
    • L2: pullback().
    • Level (source: Bill Williams, Trading Chaos; fxssi.com): stop at the nearest opposing fractal → fractals.low_level{-1} (long) / fractals.high_level{-1} (short). No fixed target (Alligator exit).

    6. Regime family

    6.1 regime_confirmed_trend — profile TR

    • L1: LONG daily trending and daily bullish and not mixed and bars_since_change > 5 and h4 bullish and ema20 > ema50 and close > ema50; SHORT mirrored on the bearish side.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Elder Triple Screen; Wilder ADX; Kaufman): no intrinsic level — across the sources the stop is a trailing / money-management overlay, not a price computed from the trend/regime features. Tuned config stop/target.

    7. Session family

    7.1 vwap_continuation — profile IN

    • L1: LONG close{-1} > vwap{-1} and low{-1} <= vwap{-1} and close{-1} > open{-1}; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: intraday() — 50% partial at +1R, force-flat at 20:00 UTC.
    • Level (source: Brian Shannon, anchored-VWAP framework; alphatrends.net): stop beyond the extreme of the bar that held VWAP → low{-1} (long) / high{-1} (short). No fixed target (ride with VWAP).

    7.2 vwap_reversion — profile IN

    • L1: stretched = abs(close{-1} − vwap{-1}) > 1.5·atr{-1}; LONG stretched and close < vwap and close > open; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: intraday().
    • Level (source: VWAP standard-deviation fade practice; bookmap.com, SMB): target = VWAP → vwap{-1} (the mean the fade reverts to). The stop stays on the config default — the ~3σ→ATR translation is a derived analogy, not a quoted figure.

    8. Cross-asset family (base ETHUSDT, context BTCUSDT)

    8.1 dual_momentum — profile TR

    • L1: LONG base_roc63 > 0 and base_roc21 > 0 and base_roc63 > context_roc63; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Gary Antonacci, Dual Momentum Investing, GEM): no intrinsic level — GEM replaces stops with the periodic momentum-sign / ranking re-evaluation (the Layer-1 flip). Tuned config stop/target.

    8.2 relative_strength_leader — profile TR

    • L1: LONG base_roc63 > context_roc63 and (base−context) spread widening; SHORT mirrored.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Levy, 1967; Faber, 2010): no intrinsic level — rank-and-hold with rebalancing, no per-position stop. Tuned config stop/target.

    8.3 context_risk_on — profile TR

    • L1: LONG context_close > context_ema200 (risk-on) and ema20 > ema50 and close > ema50; SHORT mirrored in risk-off.
    • L2: trend_rider().
    • Level (source: Faber, Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation): no intrinsic level — the regime filter exits to cash on the flip; no per-trade stop. Tuned config stop/target.

    9. Notes and caveats

    • Sizing interaction. A structural stop is often tighter or wider than the tuned default, so it changes the per-trade risk distance and therefore risk-based position size. This is intended — the stop now reflects the strategy's own invalidation level rather than a one-size default.
    • Bolted-on time-stops (6 / 24 / 8 bars) and the 20:00 UTC force-flat are generic profile machinery, not part of the canonical definitions. The close-reason evidence and the per-strategy research in §11 show both hurt: the 20:00 flat has no basis on 24/7 crypto (0 of 51 strategies justify it) and the fixed time-stops close trades at a near-zero win rate.
    • Source confidence. Most stop/target rules map to a named primary source at high or medium confidence. The two lowest-confidence cases (distance_from_ema_reversion, volatility_contraction_expansion) use the structural range-window level rather than an invented multiplier.

    10. Fidelity — canonical vs compromise

    How faithful each strategy is to its canonical source, and what (if anything) stands between it and a fully faithful implementation. There are three kinds of gap.

    10.1 Faithful — no gap

    Already matching the canon: ema_crossover, sma_regime_cross, ema200_pullback_continuation, supertrend_flip, parabolic_sar_reversal, bollinger_squeeze_breakout. (Supertrend and Parabolic SAR are the cleanest: the indicator line is the trailing stop, exactly the canonical stop-and-reverse mechanic.)

    10.2 Gap = a rule not yet authored (expressible today, no new indicator)

    The large majority. The strategy's entry and its structural level are faithful; what is missing is an explicit CLOSE rule on the strategy's own canonical exit condition (the opposite signal / oscillator recross / opposite channel), which today is only approximated by the engine's implicit flip on a fresh opposite-side entry (a stricter, slower condition) plus the tuned stop/target. CLOSE is fully authorable now — the profile's own time-stop already emits action: CLOSE — so e.g. position_side_long{-1} == 1 and rsi{-1} >= 70 → CLOSE expresses the canonical RSI exit directly. This is the bulk of §11's per-strategy recommendations (Turtle's dedicated 20-bar exit channel, DI reversal, PPO/TRIX opposite cross, the oscillator recrosses, the momentum-leg sign flip, the regime-flag flip, …). Nothing is missing from the engine; the rules were simply never written.

    10.3 Gap = a missing feature (a new indicator column — mostly pure math)

    A handful need a new feature computed to be fully canonical. All but one are pure mathematics and cheap to build; none rely on subjective judgement (fractals, which sound fuzzy, are already implemented as a mechanical 5-bar pattern):

    • linreg channel bands (linreg_slope_breakout) — the regression line ± k·(std of residuals). We already compute the line and slope; the bands are one more formula. Pure math.
    • VWAP standard-deviation bands (vwap_reversion) — VWAP ± k·(volume-weighted std of price). We already compute VWAP. Pure math.
    • Alligator (fractal_breakout_retest entry filter) — three smoothed moving averages (13/8/5) displaced forward (8/5/3). Pure math; only care needed on the forward displacement to stay causal.
    • z-score half-life estimator (zscore_reversion_to_mean adaptive time budget) — an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck AR(1) regression over the same 50-bar window to size the time-stop as ~3–4× the half-life. Pure math.
    • volume distribution-day count (volume_impulse_breakout secondary exit) — a rolling count of above-average-volume down bars after the breakout. Pure math.
    • opening-range / session-anchored levels (nr7 canonical ORB entry) — the math is trivial, but 24/7 crypto has no session, so it needs a session-anchor decision (e.g. the UTC day open) — the same question the 20:00 flat raises.
    • VCP multi-contraction detection (volatility_contraction_expansion) — detecting a sequence of progressively tighter pullbacks with volume dry-up. This is the one genuinely fuzzy / pattern feature, not a clean formula; the current percentile-of-volatility squeeze is a rough proxy.

    10.4 Gap = authoring / design choice (horizon, cadence, sizing) — not a hard engine limit

    The momentum and cross-asset family (time_series_momentum, multi_horizon_momentum, mtf_momentum_stack, dual_momentum, relative_strength_leader, context_risk_on) is where the current implementation is furthest from its canon, but — importantly — none of it is a hard engine limit. It breaks into three separable choices:

    1. Horizon (an authoring choice, fully expressible today). Their canon is a long horizon (weeks to a month). The engine already supports it two ways: higher-timeframe features — the timeframe system recognizes 1m … 1d, 1w, 1M, 1Y, BTCUSDT has 1w/1d data on disk, the engine aligns any higher timeframe onto the 5m grid, and several strategies already read 1d/4h — or a large-N window on the base timeframe (avg/roc over N bars, bounded by the spec's window_size, already used up to 260). The current authoring uses short 5m windows (roc 21/63/126 ≈ hours), which is why these strategies whipsaw; a strategy should declare its own horizon (e.g. a 1d/1w momentum feature, or a large window) rather than inherit a short 5m one. This is a per-strategy authoring decision, not an engine gap.
    2. Cadence (a design choice). The canon re-decides slowly (monthly), whereas the engine evaluates every 5m bar. Acting less often is expressible as a decision-cadence gate (act only every N bars, or only when a new higher-timeframe bar closes). Not yet wired, but authorable.
    3. Sizing (a modest risk-manager feature). The canon sizes by volatility target (each position carries equal volatility, via ATR) rather than the current stop-distance risk_based sizing. This is a clean, opt-in fourth position_sizing_method alongside fixed | risk_based | kelly — a bounded risk-manager addition, not something the engine structurally cannot do.

    With the spread/pairs z-score reversion not among the 51 (it needs two-leg coordinated execution and was never implemented), there is effectively no hard structural engine limit left among the 51 strategies — every remaining compromise is a rule to author, a mathematical feature to build (§10.3), or a horizon / timeframe to choose here.

    10.5 Entry mechanics adapted (faithful in spirit, simplified in the trigger)

    Distinct from the gaps above, five strategies keep a faithful level/exit but simplify the canonical entry: adx_di_surge (dropped Wilder's "hold beyond the signal-bar extreme" confirmation), dmi_pullback_continuation (a continuation entry rather than Wilder's DI-cross entry), fractal_breakout_retest (close+retest rather than a stop-order beyond the fractal with an Alligator filter), nr7_breakout (close beyond the prior bar rather than Crabel's opening-range stretch order), consecutive_bar_exhaustion (a Keltner-extreme gate rather than Connors' 200-period MA filter). Each is a deliberate, mostly-cheap simplification, not an engine limit.

    11. Holding time and exit timing

    The single most damaging finding of the executed campaign is that arbitrary time-based exits closed the most trades at a near-total loss. Exit-code breakdown of the 63,605 closed trades of the executed rule_lab_catalog_2024 campaign (50 full backtests):

    Exit code Trades Total PnL Avg hold Win rate
    TAKE_PROFIT 13,313 +$156,793 237 min 97%
    REDUCE 6,175 +$7,210 390 min 100%
    TRAILING_STOP 2,156 −$11,256 413 min 0%
    FLAT_AT_TIME (20:00 UTC) 2,909 −$6,691 45 min 10%
    STOP_LOSS 19,241 −$221,258 178 min 0%
    RULE_EXIT (profile time-stops) 19,811 −$76,424 66 min 0.16%

    The two arbitrary time exits — the fixed bar-count time-stops (RULE_EXIT) and the 20:00 UTC session force-flat (FLAT_AT_TIME) — together closed 22,720 trades for −$83,115 at a near-zero win rate. The time-stops in particular cut trades at ~66 minutes almost always at a loss (0.16% win): they guillotine positions long before the thesis can play out.

    11.1 What the canon says about holding time

    Across all 51 strategies the research is nearly unanimous:

    • A session force-flat does not belong on 24/7 crypto. Of the 51, zero have a canonical basis for a session-close flat — crypto has no session close. The 20:00 UTC flat is an equities concept imported by mistake and is removed for all strategies. (Genuinely intraday-VWAP strategies still exit on their stop / VWAP target / opposite signal, just not on a clock.)
    • Fixed bar-count time-stops are not part of almost any canonical definition. The classical systems end a trade on a condition — the opposite channel/signal/oscillator recross, or a volatility stop — not on a timer. The fixed 6 / 24 / 8-bar cutoffs were bolted on "by eye" and are disconnected from each strategy's own lookback.

    11.2 The adaptable principle (replacing the fixed timers)

    Instead of a fixed bar count, exit timing should follow, in order of preference:

    1. The strategy's own canonical exit condition, authored as an explicit CLOSE (§10.2) — self-adapting, because it lasts exactly as long as the setup holds.
    2. The structural stop (wired in this catalog) as the hard invalidation floor.
    3. Only if a stall cutoff is still wanted, make it relative to the strategy's own window and to volatility, not a shared constant — e.g. a breakout with a 15-bar lookback cuts at ~a fraction/multiple of 15 bars; a mean-reversion trade cuts at a multiple of its band/z-score window or of its estimated mean-reversion half-life (ATR- and lookback-scaled), which adapts automatically per symbol and timeframe.

    The per-strategy detail below records, for each strategy, what its source says about holding horizon, what governs its exit, and the criterious recommendation on 24/7 crypto at a 5m timeframe.

    11.3 Per-strategy canonical holding and exit timing

    Trend / breakout

    • donchian_breakout — canonical hold: Richard Donchian's channel breakout (the basis of the later Turtle System 1, 20-day entry / 10-day exit) was run on daily/weekly bars and held for as long as the trend kept making new channel extremes — typically days to a few weeks, no calendar limit. Translated to a 5m 20-bar entry channel on 24/7 crypto, the intent is 'hold while price keeps respecting the 20-bar channel', which on 5m could still mean many hours to days, not a fixed handful of bars. Governed by: The opposite (tighter) Donchian band, e.g. Turtle System 1's paired 20-in/10-out channels, or a 2N ATR stop. Time is not part of the definition. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Replace the current breakout() profile's fixed 6-bar no-follow-through time-stop with a structural CLOSE on the opposite, tighter channel: close{-1} < lowest(low{-10:-2}) for a long (half the entry lookback, mirroring the Turtle System-1 20/10 convention), short mirror on the high side. Keep the existing 2N ATR stop as the hard floor. If a stall cutoff is still wanted, scale it to the entry lookback (~ lookback/2 bars) rather than a fixed constant shared with other lookback lengths. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The opposite-channel exit is fully expressible today with the same lowest()/highest() primitives already used for the entry rules; donchian_breakout_spec currently has no CLOSE rule at all and instead relies on the generic breakout() profile's fixed 6-bar time-stop, which is not part of Donchian's or the Turtle System 1 definition.
    • adx_di_surge — canonical hold: Wilder's Directional Movement System (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978) holds a position for the entire life of the DI dominance — no calendar horizon is specified; a trade can run from a few bars to a very long trend. On 5m crypto this means: hold while +DI/-DI dominance and elevated ADX persist, which can be anywhere from tens to thousands of bars depending on the trend. Governed by: The DI crossover reversing (dominant DI flips) and/or Wilder's Extreme Point Rule stop (the crossover-bar's high/low as the protective stop, already implemented via long_stop_expr/short_stop_expr). No time-based exit exists in Wilder's own description. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop. Add an explicit CLOSE when the DI dominance reverses (minus_di crosses above plus_di for a long, and vice versa) or when ADX turns down after being elevated (adx{-1} < adx{-5} while adx{-1} < 25), in addition to the existing Extreme Point stop. This lets the trade end when Wilder's own signal ends rather than only on a slower full opposite-entry re-trigger. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — adx.plus_di / adx.minus_di / adx.adx are already computed features used by the entry rules; adx_di_surge_spec has no explicit exit/CLOSE rule of its own and relies purely on trend_rider's break-even/pyramid management plus the engine's implicit flip on a fresh opposite-side entry signal (which requires the full, stricter re-entry condition, not just the DI cross reversing).
    • ema_crossover — canonical hold: The dual moving-average crossover (the generic trend-following building block behind golden/death crosses and most MA-pair systems) holds a position for the entire duration between one crossover and the next opposite crossover — inherently trend-length, unspecified in bars or calendar time. On 5m crypto with a 20/50 EMA pair this can range from tens to several hundred bars depending on how long the trend persists. Governed by: The opposite EMA crossover (fast recrosses back through slow) plus, in this spec's case, the ADX>20 filter governing entry validity only. No time-based exit is part of the crossover definition. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop. This strategy is already reasonably faithful: trend_rider's engine-level handling of the opposite entry signal (cross_down closing/reversing the long) already implements the canonical 'hold until opposite cross' exit. If a stall cutoff is desired for a trend that stalls without crossing, scale it to the slow EMA period (e.g., cut only after > ~2x the slow EMA period with no progress), never a small fixed bar count. Gap: already faithful — trend_rider() with no time_stop already matches the canonical 'hold until opposite crossover' behavior; the ADX filter is an entry-quality gate, not an exit mechanism, so it does not conflict with the canon.
    • sma_regime_cross — canonical hold: The golden cross / death cross (50/200 SMA) is a regime filter, not a trade trigger, in its original and most common usage — historically applied on daily bars and held for weeks to months (position-trading horizon) since the signal itself is rare and slow-moving. Translated to 5m crypto, a 50/200-period cross on 5m bars is still a slow regime signal (200 bars ≈ 16.7 hours of coverage in the SMA window itself, but the regime it flags typically persists far longer); it is explicitly NOT meant to be held for a handful of bars. Governed by: The opposite cross (death cross exits a golden-cross long) or, per some practitioners, using the cross only as a risk-reduction/hedging trigger rather than a hard exit. No time-based exit in the canon. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop — a time-stop actively contradicts the regime-holding intent of this signal. Rely on the opposite cross (already handled by the engine's implicit flip on the entry rules) plus the tuned protective stop/take-profit config. If any stall cutoff must exist for risk-control reasons, it should be very large relative to the 200-period slow SMA (multiples of 200 bars), effectively a backstop, not a management rule. Gap: already faithful — trend_rider() with no time_stop already matches the canonical hold-until-opposite-cross behavior for this strategy; there is no session-flat or fixed time-stop currently applied to sma_regime_cross_spec.
    • triple_ema_alignment — canonical hold: The closest documented canon is Daryl Guppy's Multiple Moving Average (GMMA) ribbon: a full 12-EMA (6 short/6 long) system where a position is held while the short-term ribbon stays fanned out above (below) the long-term ribbon, and exited only when the ribbons compress or cross. This spec is a simplified 3-EMA (10/20/50) version of that same 'stacked EMA implies trend' logic. Holding horizon is trend-length — GMMA literature describes multi-week to multi-month holds on daily charts; on 5m crypto this scales to holding while the 10/20/50 stack and rising-slope condition remain intact, which can be many hours to days. Governed by: Loss of stack alignment: the short group crossing back below the mid/long group, or the ribbon compressing — not a calendar or bar-count exit. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop. Add an explicit, earlier CLOSE than the current full opposite-entry re-trigger: close when cross_down(ema_fast, ema_mid) occurs (first sign of ribbon compression), rather than waiting for the full reversed condition (fast<mid<slow AND slope(slow)<0 AND close<fast) to fire a fresh opposite entry. This mirrors GMMA's own 'short group crosses below long group' exit trigger and ends the trade materially earlier than the current implicit-flip mechanic. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — ema_fast/ema_mid/ema_slow are already computed features used by the entry rules; triple_ema_alignment_spec has no CLOSE rule and relies solely on trend_rider's implicit flip-on-opposite-entry, which requires clearing a much stricter (and later) bar than a simple ribbon-compression signal.
    • turtle_breakout — canonical hold: Turtle Trading System 2 (55-day entry channel), documented in Curtis Faith's Way of the Turtle (2007) and the original Turtle rules (Michael Covel, The Complete TurtleTrader), was run on daily bars and held for weeks — the original Turtles' average winning trade ran considerably longer than their average losing trade, with no calendar limit; duration is purely trend-length. On 5m crypto, a 55-bar entry channel is a much shorter real-time window than the original daily 55-day channel, so the 'weeks' holding intent must be re-derived from the exit-channel mechanic itself, not assumed to still mean weeks. Governed by: Turtle System 2's own paired, SHORTER exit channel: a 20-day opposite Donchian breakout, distinct from the 55-day entry channel — or the 2N ATR stop, whichever triggers first. Time is not part of the definition. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): This strategy has the clearest gap in the family: implement Turtle System 2's own 20-bar exit channel, distinct from the 55-bar entry channel it currently reuses for its implicit opposite-signal flip. Add CLOSE on close{-1} < lowest(low{-20:-2}) for a long (mirror for short) alongside the existing 2N ATR stop. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — turtle_breakout_spec only sets the entry breakout (55-bar) and the 2N stop via trend_rider; it has no CLOSE rule at all, so the position currently only exits via the 2N stop or a fresh opposite 55-bar signal — far slower and wider than the canonical dedicated 20-bar exit channel that defines Turtle System 2's actual exit timing.
    • aroon_trend_emergence — canonical hold: Tushar Chande's Aroon indicator (The New Technical Trader, 1994) is designed to catch a trend at its 'dawn' (Aroon meaning 'dawn's early light' in Sanskrit) and ride it while the dominant Aroon line stays pinned near the 70-100 extreme — no calendar horizon; duration is however long the emergence/momentum phase lasts. On 5m crypto this means holding while the 25-bar Aroon-up (or down) stays elevated and rising, which can range from tens to hundreds of bars. Governed by: The dominant Aroon line declining off the 70-100 extreme, or an Aroon crossover reversal (the opposite line crossing back above the dominant one) — a structural, indicator-driven exit, not a time-based one. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop. Add an explicit CLOSE when the dominant Aroon line falls out of its 70+ zone after having been there (e.g., aroon.up{-1} < 70 having previously been >= 70, or aroon.up{-1} < aroon.up{-5} while aroon.down{-1} is rising) rather than relying only on trend_rider's implicit flip on a fresh, stricter opposite-side entry. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — aroon.up / aroon.down are already computed features used by the entry rules; aroon_trend_emergence_spec has no CLOSE rule and relies solely on trend_rider's implicit opposite-entry flip, which requires clearing the full, stricter opposite-side condition rather than reacting to the earlier 'declining off the extreme' signal Chande describes as the exit warning.
    • linreg_slope_breakout — canonical hold: Unlike Turtle/Wilder/Donchian, linear-regression-channel breakout is a modern quant-trading construct with no single authoritative book source; it is consistently documented across algorithmic-trading references as: enter on a channel-band break with a slope filter, hold while the trend/slope persists, and exit on reversion to the regression midline. There is no calendar holding period specified — duration is tied to how long price stays away from the regression mean. On 5m crypto with a 50-bar regression window, this means holding for a horizon proportional to that window, not a fixed handful of bars. Governed by: Price crossing back through the regression midline (mean-reversion exit) or the regression slope flipping sign — not a fixed time. Some documented variants use a trailing EMA stop instead, but a fixed bar-count time-stop is not part of any documented variant. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Replace the breakout() profile's fixed 6-bar no-follow time-stop with a structural CLOSE when close crosses back through the regression line itself (close{-1} recrossing linreg.value{-1} against the trade direction), or when slope(linreg.value{-10:-1}) flips sign. If a stall cutoff must remain, scale it to the regression window (e.g., ~window/5 bars, i.e. 10 bars for the current 50-bar window) instead of a fixed constant shared with unrelated strategies. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — linreg.value and its slope are already computed features used by the entry rules; linreg_slope_breakout_spec has no CLOSE rule of its own and instead inherits the generic breakout() profile's fixed 6-bar time-stop, which does not correspond to any documented variant of this strategy.
    • ema200_pullback_continuation — canonical hold: Alexander Elder's Triple Screen Trading System matches this strategy's structure closely: a long-term trend filter (here, the daily 200 EMA), an intermediate pullback signal (here, the base-timeframe EMA20 tag with RSI confirmation, standing in for Elder's oscillator-based Screen 2), and a short-term execution stop (Screen 3). Elder describes holding these trades for days on a daily-chart execution screen, with duration governed by how long the pullback takes to resolve (continue or fail), not a calendar limit. Governed by: A protective stop beyond the pullback swing (Elder places it a tick beyond the trade-day/prior-day extreme — already implemented here via the lowest(low{-3:-1})/highest(high{-3:-1}) swing stop), moved to break-even once in profit, then a progressive profit target. No time-based exit in Elder's own description. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop needed; the current swing-stop already matches Elder's Screen 3 stop-placement rule. If a stall cutoff is wanted for a pullback that neither continues nor stops out, scale it to the EMA20 lookback (~20 bars) rather than borrowing a fixed constant from another strategy's profile. Gap: already faithful — pullback() already applies no time-stop and no session-flat to this strategy; the existing swing-based stop already matches Elder's Screen 3 stop-placement convention, and no fixed time-stop or 20:00 UTC force-flat is currently applied here.
    • supertrend_flip — canonical hold: The Supertrend indicator (Olivier Seban, Everybody Deserves to be Rich) is explicitly an 'always-in-the-market' stop-and-reverse system: the trader is never flat, holding long or short for as long as price stays on that side of the line — from a handful of bars in a choppy market to a very long run in a strong trend. There is no calendar horizon in the definition; duration is whatever the line-flip interval turns out to be. Governed by: The Supertrend line itself flipping (price closing on the opposite side of the line) — this is both the trailing stop and the reversal signal in one mechanic. Time is not part of the definition at all. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): None needed — this is already the most faithful strategy in the family. trend_rider's _line_trail mechanic (the Supertrend line IS the stop, tightening every bar and closing the trade when price crosses it) already implements the canonical stop-and-reverse behavior exactly. Explicitly exclude this strategy from any global fixed time-stop or session-flat retrofit, since either would break its defining always-in-the-market property. Gap: already faithful — supertrend_flip_spec's action_rules (trend_rider with long_stop_line_expr/short_stop_line_expr) already implement the canonical line-is-the-stop, stop-and-reverse mechanic faithfully; no time-stop or session-flat is currently applied.
    • ichimoku_cloud_breakout — canonical hold: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo (Goichi Hosoda, published 1969) was designed around Japan's traditional trading-month convention (its default 9/26/52 parameters derive from a 26-trading-day month) for daily-chart swing trading, with trades intended to run for weeks. There is no explicit calendar exit in the method; duration is governed by how long the cloud breakout and Kijun-based structure hold. On 5m crypto the tenkan/kijun/cloud parameters keep their bar-count meaning but the 'trading month' rationale for the default lookbacks does not carry over literally — the exit logic (below) is what should be preserved, not the specific day-count parameters. Governed by: Price crossing back through the Kijun-sen (or a Tenkan/Kijun cross reversal), or price re-entering/breaking back into the cloud. The near cloud edge (already implemented as the stop here) and the Kijun line are the two structural levels the canon actually manages the trade against — not time. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard time-stop. Add an explicit CLOSE when close crosses back through the kijun line against the trade direction (close{-1} crosses_down kijun{-1} for a long, mirror for short), in addition to the existing near-cloud-edge stop. This gives a materially faster, canonical exit trigger instead of waiting for the full opposite-entry condition (cloud break + tenkan/kijun cross + 26-bar lagging-span confirmation) to clear. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — ichimoku.kijun is already a computed feature used by the entry rules (via tenkan/kijun comparison); ichimoku_cloud_breakout_spec has no CLOSE rule and relies solely on trend_rider's implicit flip on a fresh, much stricter opposite-entry signal.

    Momentum

    • time_series_momentum — canonical hold: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', use a 12-month trailing-return sign signal held for a 1-month rebalance period, i.e. the position is simply kept (or flipped) at the next monthly rebalance based on the trailing-return sign; the paper's holding horizon is 'until next rebalance', not a fixed small bar count. On this codebase's 5m bars the two return legs are roc_63 (~5.25h) and roc_21 (~1.75h) -- already a heavily compressed, intraday analogue of the 12-month/1-month TSMOM signal, not the literal horizon. No genuine time-based exit exists in the canon; the monthly cadence in the original paper is a data/rebalance-frequency artifact of the study, not a rule about how long a trade must be held. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard bar-count time-stop. Add an explicit CLOSE when the medium-horizon leg (roc_63) flips sign against the open position -- this is the DSL equivalent of the canonical 'exit at sign-flip'. Today the position instead only unwinds via the config stop/take-profit or an opposite ENTRY signal firing; there is no direct CLOSE tied to the signal decaying. If a stall-cut is wanted at all, size it to the slower leg (~63 bars) rather than an arbitrary fixed count.
