Size the stall time-stop off the 20-bar EMA period (e.g. ~1.5-2x = 30-40 bars) instead of the current flat 24. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The EMA target is correctly authored, but no structural stop expression is set (long_stop_expr/short_stop_expr are both omitted), so the stop falls back to the generic tuned config instead of the canon's ATR-relative placement beyond the stretch extreme; the 24-bar time-stop is also disconnected from the 20-bar EMA period the strategy reads.

    Volatility / structure

    • failed_breakout_reversal — canonical hold: Canon is Connors & Raschke's 'Turtle Soup' fade of a failed 20-bar breakout (Street Smarts, 1995) -- the setup here (close beyond a 20-bar extreme then closing back inside) is the Turtle Soup entry almost verbatim. Raschke's own guidance is a fast countertrend scalp: close the position 2-3 bars after entry, or use a floating stop toward the range. On 24/7 5m crypto this means 'a small fraction of the 20-bar setup lookback,' not a fixed constant unrelated to the setup. Governed by: A timed exit (2-3 bars) OR a floating/trailing stop back toward the range midpoint -- Turtle Soup does not wait for a new opposite signal, it is a scalp against the failed break. A time component IS part of the canonical definition here, but it is meant to be proportional to the entry lookback (20 bars), not an arbitrary constant. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Replace the current fixed 8-bar failure_reversal time-stop with a lookback-relative one: hold at most N bars where N is a small fraction of the entry lookback W (e.g. N ~ 0.10-0.15 * W = 2-3 bars for W=20), and add a floating exit toward the range midpoint, e.g. CLOSE when price reaches avg(highest(high{-20:-3}), lowest(low{-20:-3})) before the timer expires. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The floating/trailing stop toward the mid-range is not wired; only the fixed failure-wick stop and a flat 8-bar/0R time-stop exist today.
    • inside_bar_expansion — canonical hold: Canon is Toby Crabel's narrow-range/inside-day breakout patterns (Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout, 1990) -- a day-trading pattern meant to be entered and exited within the same trading day, i.e. a short hold measured in a handful of bars, not days. Governed by: Momentum stall or a reversal back into the mother bar's range (structural invalidation); Crabel's day-trading context implies same-day exit but does not define a bar-count time-stop as the mechanism -- the failure mode is re-entry into the compressed range, not the clock. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Drop the flat 6-bar no-follow-through cut; add an explicit structural CLOSE when price re-enters the mother bar's range (close{-1} back between low{-3} and high{-3}), and scale any stall check to the mother bar's own range relative to current ATR (e.g. cut only if unrealized progress has not reached ~1x mother-bar range within roughly mother_bar_range/ATR bars). Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — Re-entry into the mother bar as an explicit CLOSE condition is expressible today (compare close to bar -3's high/low) but is not authored; only the initial breakout() stop and the generic fixed time-stop exist.
    • atr_expansion_breakout — canonical hold: This is a generic ATR-confirmed channel breakout in the Donchian/Turtle-System lineage (Wilder's ATR from New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978, combined with channel-breakout trend-following). Canonically trend-following: held as long as the trend persists (days to weeks on the original daily-bar systems), not a fixed bar count. Governed by: Opposite/shorter channel breakout (e.g. Turtle System's exit on the 10-day low after a 20-day-high entry) and/or a volatility trailing stop -- time is not part of the canonical mechanism. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Remove the flat 6-bar no-follow time-stop; exit on a shorter opposite-channel breakout (e.g. close < lowest(low{-5:-2}) for a long, using roughly half the 10-bar entry channel, Turtle-style asymmetric channel) or opt into the existing trail_atr_mult (>=2 ATR) wide protective trail already supported by the breakout() profile instead of a hard timer. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The opposite/shorter-channel exit is expressible today with the same lowest/highest window primitives used for entry, but no such CLOSE rule is wired; the strategy currently only has the fixed no-follow time-stop and no trailing/opposite-channel exit.
    • volatility_contraction_expansion — canonical hold: Canon is Mark Minervini's Volatility Contraction Pattern (Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard, 2013 / Think & Trade Like a Champion). A swing/position trade meant to run for weeks to months while trend structure holds -- explicitly NOT time-boxed; multiple contractions can occur before the resolving breakout. Governed by: A structural trailing stop (a rising short/medium moving average or the most recent higher-low swing) plus a hard percentage stop (7-8% initial risk); partials taken into strength around 2-3R. No time-based exit in the source. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Remove the flat 6-bar no-follow cut entirely for this strategy -- VCP explicitly tolerates a stalled-but-unbroken position across several contraction legs. Keep only the structural stop (below the contraction low, already implemented) and trail via a rising short EMA or the swing-low structure as profit accrues, matching the existing partial_reduce logic. Gap: needs a new feature/indicator — True VCP requires detecting a sequence of progressively tightening contraction legs plus volume dry-up ahead of the breakout; the current rule only checks a single-level percentile-of-volatility squeeze, not the multi-contraction sequence Minervini's pattern is defined by.
    • parabolic_sar_reversal — canonical hold: Wilder's Parabolic SAR (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978) is held until price crosses the SAR dot -- no fixed period at all; the accelerating SAR itself adapts the effective hold to trend strength. Governed by: The SAR flip itself: the line IS both the trailing stop and the stop-and-reverse signal. Genuinely a signal-based (not time-based) exit, and Wilder recommends filtering entries/exits with ADX > 20-25 (already done here via the adx.adx > 20 entry gate). Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No change needed: the existing trend_rider(long_stop_line_expr=sar) management with no time-stop already IS the criterious, volatility-adaptive exit the canon prescribes. Gap: already faithful — The current implementation (SAR line trail via trend_rider, no time-stop, ADX>20 filter) already matches Wilder's canonical stop-and-reverse mechanic.
    • choppiness_release — canonical hold: The Choppiness Index (created by Australian trader E.W. Dreiss) is a regime filter, not a trade system with its own holding-period prescription; its Fibonacci thresholds (38.2 / 61.8) classify trending vs. choppy regimes. The resulting breakout trade is meant to be held as long as the market stays in the efficient/directional regime the release identified. Governed by: No source-defined trade exit exists; the criterious analog is symmetric with the entry -- exit or tighten when choppiness reverts back above the choppy threshold (regime reversal), alongside the structural breakout stop. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Replace the flat 6-bar no-follow cut with a CHOP-based regime exit: CLOSE (or tighten) when chop{-1} > 61.8 recurs -- the directional regime the breakout relied on has evaporated -- keeping a trailing stop for as long as the trend itself persists. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — A CLOSE rule keyed on choppiness recrossing back above the choppy threshold is expressible today with the already-built choppiness feature but is not wired into action_rules.
    • dmi_pullback_continuation — canonical hold: Wilder's Directional Movement System with the Extreme Point Rule (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978): trend-following, held as long as the directional trend persists -- exit happens exactly when +DI/-DI cross in the opposite direction, which can be an extended hold with no fixed period. Governed by: The DI crossover (opposite signal) is the canonical exit; between entry and that crossover, the Extreme Point Rule pins the stop at the crossover bar's own extreme (already matched here: the pullback bar's low/high is used as the stop). Genuinely signal-based, not time-based. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No time-stop; add a CLOSE rule on the DI lines crossing in the opposite direction (adx.minus_di{-1} > adx.plus_di{-1} for a long, and the mirror for a short) using the already-built ADX feature -- this is the one missing piece versus an otherwise-faithful management (pullback() correctly carries no time-stop today). Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The DI-crossover CLOSE condition is expressible today with the existing DMI/ADX feature but is not authored into pullback()'s action_rules for this strategy; the position currently only exits via config stop/take-profit/trailing.
    • regime_switch_hybrid — canonical hold: Not a single named canonical strategy -- it is an ensemble of a classic dual-EMA trend-following system and a Wilder-style RSI overbought/oversold fade, gated by a trend/range regime classifier (conceptually the practitioner analog of Markov regime-switching frameworks such as Hamilton's). Holding horizon depends on the active leg: the trend leg is meant to run until the trend reverses (no fixed period); the range leg is a fast RSI mean-reversion swing meant to close on reversion. Governed by: Trend leg: the EMA(fast/slow) crossing back or price re-crossing the slow EMA. Range leg: RSI recrossing the opposite extreme or the midline. Either leg is also invalidated if the daily regime flag itself flips away from the regime that licensed the trade. None of this is time-based. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No fixed time-stop; add a CLOSE keyed on the regime flag flipping (trending{-1} == 0 for the trend leg, ranging{-1} == 0 for the range leg) and/or the RSI recross (e.g. rsi{-1} < 50 for a range-leg long) so the exit is exactly as adaptive as the entry's own regime/oscillator logic. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — regime_hybrid() currently has no CLOSE rule tied to the regime flag or to an EMA/RSI recross; only break-even, pyramiding and config-driven exits exist.
    • bollinger_squeeze_breakout — canonical hold: John Bollinger's BandWidth squeeze (Bollinger on Bollinger Bands, 2001): meant to run as long as price 'walks the band' -- an extended trend hold, not time-boxed. Bollinger explicitly treats a band tag as informational only, not itself an exit trigger. Governed by: A close back through the middle band (the 20-period basis) is Bollinger's standard 'the walk is over' signal -- this strategy already implements exactly that as its structural stop (bb.middle). No time-based exit in the source. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Keep the existing middle-band stop as the primary exit (already faithful); the residual issue is the shared breakout() profile's generic fixed 6-bar no-follow-through time-stop layered on top, which is extraneous to Bollinger's own rule -- a squeeze breakout can legitimately consolidate at the band edge for several bars before walking, so this time-stop should be loosened or removed for this strategy rather than left at a flat constant. Gap: already faithful — The core exit mechanism (close back through the middle band) already matches the canon; the only friction is the generic profile-level 6-bar time-stop that is not specific to this strategy's own logic.
    • bollinger_keltner_squeeze — canonical hold: John Carter's TTM Squeeze (Mastering the Trade, ch. 11, 2005): held while the momentum histogram keeps expanding in the trade's direction -- an explicitly momentum-defined hold, typically a handful of bars but sized by the histogram's own behavior, not a fixed bar count or a fixed profit multiple. Governed by: Carter's rule of thumb is to exit/take profit after two consecutive momentum-histogram bars decelerating in the trade's direction (e.g. two dark-blue bars after light-blue bars for a long) -- a momentum-color-change exit, not a fixed ATR target. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Replace/augment the current fixed +2 ATR 'first staged target' with a momentum-deceleration exit using the already-built ROC feature: e.g. CLOSE (or partial) when roc{-1} < roc{-2} < roc{-3} for a long (two bars of decelerating momentum), mirrored for a short. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The two-bars-of-deceleration momentum exit is expressible today with the existing ROC feature (a closer-fidelity version would use a dedicated momentum-histogram feature, but ROC direction-change is a workable proxy); the current +2 ATR target is a practitioner substitute, not Carter's canonical rule.
    • nr7_breakout — canonical hold: Toby Crabel's NR7 breakout (Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout, 1990) is an explicit DAY-TRADING pattern on daily bars: profits are typically taken at the close of the first trading day or on the first profitable close -- a hold of essentially one full session in the original context. Governed by: A same-session exit (close of the day the breakout triggers, or first profitable close), with the stop trailed via ATR or Parabolic SAR -- genuinely session/time-anchored in the ORIGINAL daily-bar context, because Crabel's edge ('narrow day precedes an expanded day') is scoped to exactly one full session. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Set the strategy's time-stop explicitly relative to its own 7-bar lookback (e.g. flatten if not profitable within ~1-2x the 7-bar window, i.e. roughly 7-14 bars) instead of relying on the generic breakout() default of 6 bars, which happens to be close but is not derived from this strategy's own parameter. Gap: structural engine gap — Crabel's canonical anchor is one calendar trading session, which does not exist as a concept in a 24/7 continuous market -- there is no genuine session boundary to be faithful to, so the 'one session' hold cannot be reproduced exactly regardless of engine capability. The best available proxy (a lookback-relative bar-count time-stop) is expressible today, but it is an approximation of the canon, not a faithful reproduction.
    • pivot_breakout_continuation — canonical hold: Classic floor-trader pivot points (CME/CBOT floor-trading practice, codified across general TA references): held within one daily pivot cycle, since pivots are computed once per session from the prior session's high/low/close and are valid for exactly that session, targeting the next pivot level out. Governed by: The next-pivot target and a structural stop just inside the broken level (already implemented here: S1/R1 stop, R2/S2 target). Canonically the levels themselves also expire at the next daily recalculation -- a position still open when new pivots are computed is trading against stale reference levels. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Instead of a 20:00 UTC force-flat, close or re-tag the position when the daily bar underlying the pivot feature rolls over (i.e. when new R1/S1/R2/S2 values become available) -- e.g. CLOSE if unresolved by the time daily pivots recompute, or re-anchor stop/target to the newly computed levels rather than forcing flat at a fixed hour unrelated to the pivot cycle. Gap: needs a new feature/indicator — The engine has the pivot feature itself but no explicit 'new daily pivot bar available' / stale-level trigger wired as a CLOSE condition. A coarse proxy (time_hour{-1} == 0, i.e. UTC midnight) is expressible today, but a dedicated 'pivot rolled over' feature would be the precise fix.
    • fractal_breakout_retest — canonical hold: Bill Williams' Fractals within the Profitunity/Chaos system (Trading Chaos, 1995): held as long as the trend structure holds per the Alligator indicator's jaw/teeth/lips alignment -- no fixed period, can run for an extended trend. Governed by: Two canonical triggers: (1) an opposite fractal forming (reversal signal) and (2) the Alligator lines starting to converge/cross (trend exhaustion). Williams ties his exits to the Alligator indicator specifically, which this codebase does not yet build. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No time-stop; keep the existing opposing-fractal-level stop (already a reasonable partial proxy) and, once available, add a CLOSE/tighten rule on the Alligator's jaw/teeth/lips converging or crossing -- the genuinely criterious, trend-adaptive exit Williams defines. Gap: needs a new feature/indicator — The canonical exit trigger (Alligator lines crossing/converging) requires the Alligator indicator (three smoothed, forward-shifted moving averages) as a feature; it does not exist in the feature helpers yet, so the strategy currently substitutes the fractal-level stop as an incomplete proxy for the full Williams exit rule.

    Regime

    • regime_confirmed_trend — canonical hold: This strategy is a rescaled implementation of Alexander Elder's Triple Screen Trading System (Trading for a Living, 1993): a higher-timeframe 'tide' trend filter (here: daily Market State, confirmed + established >5 bars/days), an intermediate 'wave' agreement (here: 4h regime direction), and a lower-timeframe 'ripple' for entry timing (here: the 5m EMA20/EMA50 stack). Elder's canon holds a position for as long as the tide (the highest timeframe) stays intact, which in his own daily/weekly setup is days to weeks. Rescaled to this engine's daily-tide + 4h-wave + 5m-entry stack, the analogous holding horizon is however long the DAILY regime stays a confirmed, non-mixed trend in the trade's direction -- typically many hours to several days of 5m bars (hundreds to low thousands of bars), not a fixed handful of bars. Governed by: In the canon, the position is closed when the tide itself reverses or goes back into a non-trending/mixed state, when a trailing stop protects the accumulated profit as the trend runs, or when the entry-timeframe signal flips against the position. There is no fixed time-stop in Triple Screen or in general multi-timeframe trend-confirmation practice -- the trade is held exactly as long as the higher-timeframe trend that licensed it remains confirmed. Today in this codebase, regime_confirmed_trend uses the trend_rider() profile called with NO time-stop and NO session-flat argument (confirmed by reading rule_strategies/regime.py and profiles.py): its only exits are the opposite 5m EMA entry signal, the tuned config stop-loss/take-profit, break-even at +1R, and pyramiding at +2R capped at 2 legs. So a time-based exit is not part of this particular strategy's current definition at all -- it is one of the few strategies in the catalog that does NOT bolt on an arbitrary bar-count time-stop or a session-flat. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Replace 'no time-based exit at all' with a genuine regime-rollover exit, adaptive per symbol/timeframe because it rides the same self-calibrating regime features that gate entry (bars_since_regime_change_count, stability windows) rather than a hardcoded bar count: CLOSE the position when the DAILY regime that licensed it stops being confirmed -- i.e. trend_trending{-1} == 0 or mixed_regime{-1} == 1 -- or when the 4h wave flips against the held side (h4_bear{-1} == 1 while long, h4_bull{-1} == 1 while short). This makes the exit symmetric with the entry gate (same tide/wave features) and self-adapts to whatever regime persistence a given symbol/timeframe exhibits, instead of assuming a fixed number of 5m bars. Keep the existing +1R break-even and +2R pyramiding as-is (those are R-multiple, not time-based, and already fit the canon). Do not add a stalled-trade time-stop borrowed from the breakout/mean-reversion profiles (6/24/8 bars) -- that bar count has no relationship to how long a daily regime takes to prove itself and would just reintroduce an arbitrary cutoff into a strategy whose whole thesis is to ride a higher-timeframe trend. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The daily and 4h Market State features this exit would need (trend_trending, mixed_regime, dir_bullish/dir_bearish) are already computed and already merged into regime_confirmed_trend_spec's window_features for entry gating -- nothing new needs to be built. The gap is that no CLOSE action_rule re-checks them after entry: trend_rider() as called here has no exit path tied to the regime rolling over, so a position stays open purely on the config stop/take-profit and the opposite 5m EMA signal even after the daily tide that justified the trade has already turned.

    Session

    • vwap_continuation — canonical hold: The canonical technique here is Brian Shannon's Anchored VWAP (AVWAP) method (book: "Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP"; summarized at alphatrends.net). Shannon explicitly applies AVWAP across day traders, swing traders AND investors — the hold time is not fixed by the technique itself, it is however long the trend that the anchor represents keeps respecting the level. On 24/7 crypto at 5m this translates to: hold from minutes up to many hours or days, for as long as price keeps bouncing off / respecting the session VWAP in the trade direction — there is no inherent duration cap in the canon. Governed by: A structural, price-based exit: the anchored level flipping from support to resistance (or vice versa) — i.e. price closing back through VWAP against the position — combined with a protective stop beyond the extreme of the bar that held VWAP. Shannon frames management as using the level to 'cut our losers, hold our winners,' not a clock. A time-based exit is NOT part of this canon at all. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Drop the fixed 20:00 UTC session flat entirely for this strategy. Exit on whichever comes first of: (a) the existing structural stop (already correct: beyond the low/high of the bar that held VWAP), or (b) an explicit CLOSE when price closes back through VWAP against the position (the level flipping from support to resistance or vice versa — the actual trend-invalidation signal in the canon). Do not add a hard bar-count cap; if a no-follow-through filter is wanted at all, size it relative to the pattern's own lookback (e.g. cut if price hasn't moved >= 1 ATR in favor within roughly the number of bars the pullback itself spanned), not a fixed constant. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — No rule today closes the trade on a VWAP support/resistance flip against the position — the only exits are the structural stop, the config take-profit/partial, and the arbitrary 20:00 UTC flat. Everything needed (close/vwap features, position side flags) already exists.
    • vwap_reversion — canonical hold: Per practitioner VWAP-fade references (crosstrade.io's VWAP reversion writeup, HorizonAI's mean-reversion guide), a reversion trade is meant to be short and mechanical: held only until price reverts to the mean (VWAP), typically minutes to a couple of hours intraday on equities/futures — i.e. a handful of bars once the reversion actually starts moving. Guidance explicitly says to abandon a reversion trade that hasn't begun moving toward target within roughly 3-5 bars. Translated to 5m crypto: expect resolution within a similarly small number of bars once turning begins, scaled by how far price was stretched from VWAP at entry (a bigger stretch takes proportionally longer to travel back even at the same reversion speed). Governed by: Primarily the reversion target itself (price returns to VWAP) or a protective stop placed beyond the extreme that triggered the fade (commonly ~1x ATR beyond the trigger high/low, per crosstrade.io's documented VWAP-reversion stop rule). A bar-count stall exit IS a legitimate, commonly used add-on in mean-reversion practice (unlike the continuation case) because a reversion premise can simply be wrong on a trend day — but it should scale with the stretch/volatility rather than being a flat constant. Session-close liquidation appears in equities/futures reference implementations (e.g. the crosstrade.io Pine Script flattens at 3:55pm ET) only because of literal exchange-close / overnight-gap risk, not because the strategy's logic needs a clock. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): Keep the target at VWAP itself (already correct/canonical). Add a structural stop ~1x ATR beyond the entry-bar extreme (the same atr feature already computed for the stretch condition) instead of leaving the stop fully on the tuned config. Replace the fixed time_stop_bars=24 with a stretch/volatility-relative threshold instead of a flat constant — concretely, close if position_bars_since_entry{-1} >= k * (abs(position_entry_price{-1} - position_initial_take_profit{-1}) / market_atr{-1}) for a small multiplier k (~2-3), which is available today with existing position fields (position_initial_take_profit already holds the VWAP-at-entry target since it's set via entry_take_profit) and lets the cutoff shrink for a mild stretch and grow for a violent one, per symbol and timeframe automatically through market_atr. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The structural ATR-based stop is expressible today (same atr feature already used in the entry rule) but is currently left on the tuned config. The bar-count formula upgrade is also expressible today using the entry-time snapshot fields the engine already provides (position_entry_price, position_initial_take_profit, position_bars_since_entry) against the CURRENT market_atr, so no new engine feature is strictly required for a workable adaptive version. A more precise version would use the ATR at entry rather than the current bar's ATR; that snapshot does not exist yet (only entry price / initial stop / initial take-profit / bars-since-entry / R-multiple are captured per grep of modules/bot-logic/src/rainbow/bot_logic/helpers/action_rules.py), which would be a missing_feature if an exact entry-time-ATR formula is required.

    Cross-asset

    • dual_momentum — canonical hold: Antonacci's dual momentum (Global Equities Momentum) computes a 12-month lookback for both absolute and relative momentum and rebalances monthly, so each leg is held for a full month between recomputations regardless of interim drawdown — there is no intra-month stop or target in the canon. Translated to 24/7 crypto at 5m: the intent is 'hold roughly one lookback period between signal re-evaluations,' not a fixed handful of bars. On this system the base_mom lookback is roc(63) (~63 five-minute bars, ~5.25 hours) and base_fast is roc(21) (~1.75 hours), so the effective holding-horizon-by-construction is already far shorter than the canonical 'month,' independent of any exit-timing rule. Governed by: A scheduled periodic re-evaluation: at the next rebalance date the absolute and relative momentum signs are recomputed, and the position is rotated out (to cash or the other side) only if the recomputed signal no longer supports it. It is a calendar cadence, not a stop-loss, target, or trailing exit, and it is emphatically not a 'time stop' in the risk-management sense (cut a stalled/losing trade after N bars) — a winning trade can be held for many consecutive rebalance periods. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard bar-count time-stop and no session force-flat. Exit only on the same signal flipping: for the long side, close when base_mom{-1} <= 0 or base_mom{-1} <= context_mom{-1} (absolute or relative momentum loses its edge); mirror for shorts. Currently this family (trend_rider profile) already carries no time_stop and no FLAT_AT_TIME rule, which is correctly aligned with the canon — the remaining gap is that the exit is only implicit (relying on the opposite EntryRule to reverse the position) rather than an explicit CLOSE authored as the mirror of the entry condition. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — The DSL and existing features (base_mom, base_fast, context_mom) are sufficient to express a genuine flip-based exit, but cross_asset.py only defines entry_rules (LONG/SHORT market-view signals) and relies on trend_rider()'s default management (break-even, pyramid) plus whatever the engine does when the Layer-1 signal reverses or goes NONE. There is no explicit CLOSE action mirroring the entry condition, so a case where absolute momentum turns negative without the opposite side's relative-momentum condition being met yet may not be closed promptly.
    • relative_strength_leader — canonical hold: Relative-strength rotation systems (Faber, 'Relative Strength Strategies for Investing') rank a universe by trailing return (commonly 1–12 month windows, or a blended set) and hold each top-ranked asset from one periodic rebalance to the next — typically weeks to a couple of months — for as long as it keeps outranking its peers. There is no intra-period stop or target defined by the ranking mechanic itself. On 5m crypto the intent maps to: hold while the base keeps outperforming the context over the same comparison window used at entry, not for a fixed short bar count. Governed by: Periodic re-ranking / re-comparison: the position is dropped when the asset loses its relative-strength edge against the peer(s) it is being compared to (rank falls, or the return spread reverses). Some published variants add a slow trend overlay (10-month SMA) as an additional filter, but the core rotation exit is a recompute of the ranking, not a time-stop or a session boundary. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard bar-count time-stop. Close when the RS spread that drove entry rolls over — the exact mirror of the entry condition: for the long side, close when (base_mom{-1} - context_mom{-1}) < (base_mom{-5} - context_mom{-5}) turns true while base_mom{-1} < context_mom{-1} (the base has lost its lead), or more simply when base_mom{-1} <= context_mom{-1}. This keeps the exit criterion symmetric with, and adaptive to, the same 63/5-bar comparison windows already used for entry, so it scales automatically if those lookbacks are ever re-tuned per symbol/timeframe. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — Same structural gap as dual_momentum: only entry_rules are authored, and the exit relies implicitly on the opposite-side EntryRule reversing the position rather than an explicit CLOSE that fires as soon as the base's relative-strength lead is lost (which can happen well before the opposite side's stricter widening condition is met).
    • context_risk_on — canonical hold: Faber's 'A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation' uses a 10-month SMA (~200-day) regime filter that is deliberately slow: an asset stays in its risk-on or risk-off bucket for months at a time because the filter only flips a handful of times per year. The base's own faster trend read (here EMA20/50) governs the tactical entries/exits nested inside that slow regime, so holding time is naturally two-timescale: the regime persists for a long horizon while individual trades inside it are held only as long as the base's own trend structure stays intact. Governed by: Two nested, purely structural conditions, neither of which is a time-stop: (1) the base's own trend flips (ema_fast crosses ema_slow, or close crosses ema_slow against the position), or (2) the context's regime flips (context daily close crosses its 200-day EMA). Faber's rule literally is 'sell and move to cash when price crosses below the SMA' — a structural crossover exit, never a bar count. Recommended exit timing (crypto 24/7, 5m): No hard bar-count time-stop and no session force-flat. Close the position the moment either nested condition invalidates it: for the long side, close when ema_fast{-1} < ema_slow{-1} (base structure breaks) OR context_close{-1} < context_ema200{-1} (regime flips risk-off) — whichever comes first; mirror for shorts. This is adaptable per symbol/timeframe automatically because it reuses whatever EMA lengths and context timeframe the strategy is configured with, rather than a fixed bar count. Gap: authorable now (just needs a DSL close rule) — All the features needed for a faithful exit (base ema_fast, ema_slow, close, context_close, context_ema200) already exist and are already merged into window_features for the entry rules; only entry_rules are authored, so a case where the base's EMA stack breaks down while the context's daily regime hasn't flipped yet (or vice versa) is not caught by any explicit exit — the position only reverses if the opposite side's full entry condition (regime AND base structure) is met, which is stricter than either invalidation alone.
